input: Audience: Wedding-business owners with an inquiry nurture sequence who are reviewing whether follow-up content is helping couples take a next step. | Tension: A sequence may show healthy opens while some messages receive no clicks, making it easy to overstate what open rates say about buyer interest or sequence effectiveness. | Argument: Email opens can show that a message was viewed, but clicks offer a different signal about which content prompted an action. Owners can use those differences to decide which messages deserve closer review, without treating engagement as proof that the email caused a tour or booking. | Take: Review opens and clicks at the message level, inspect the content of emails associated with clicks, and keep engagement signals separate from confirmed tour or booking outcomes. | Mechanism: During a review of one venue's workflow, the team noted that some emails were opened without clicks and that clicks appeared to increase on later messages. They discussed examining the content of those emails, including a guest-entertainment guide and weather or backup-plan information, as material worth reviewing rather than proof of booking causation. | Reader decision: When reviewing your own sequence, identify which messages prompt clicks and inspect what they offer before deciding what to retain, revise, or test next.
